# Power and measurement attenuation — Project 71

**Written 2026-08-01, before B3, T or T_ctrl were scored.** Generated by
`scripts/power_analysis.py`; re-run it to reproduce every number here.

Required by the pre-lock audit. The point of writing it now is that if we are
underpowered for our own pre-registered effect, that is a **pre-registered finding**,
not something discovered after the numbers disappoint.

## 0. The headline conclusion

**We are underpowered for our pre-registered 10-point ASR effect, and the binding
constraint is judge recall (0.55), not sample size.** A true 10-point reduction is
measured as ~5.5 points and would fail our own threshold. Details and the recommended
correction are in §5.

## 1. Measurement attenuation — the dominant term

The ASR judge has precision 1.00 and **recall 0.55** (n=36, inter-model agreement —
see the label-provenance correction). With precision 1 and recall r, an arm whose true
failure rate is p is measured at `r * p`. So a true difference D is observed as
`r * D`:

| true ASR reduction | observed at r=0.45 | r=0.55 (ours) | r=0.65 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 5 pts | 2.2 | **2.8** | 3.2 |
| 10 pts | 4.5 | **5.5** | 6.5 |
| 15 pts | 6.8 | **8.2** | 9.8 |
| 20 pts | 9.0 | **11.0** | 13.0 |
| 25 pts | 11.2 | **13.8** | 16.2 |

**A true 10-point reduction — exactly our pre-registered minimum meaningful effect —
is measured as 5.5 points and therefore FAILS our own threshold.** The threshold and
the instrument are inconsistent. Either the threshold is restated on the observed
scale (a 10-point *observed* reduction implies ~18 points true), or reported effects
are attenuation-corrected with the recall CI propagated. Correcting is not free:
recall 0.55 has 95% CI [0.29, 0.76] from n=36, so dividing by it inflates the
interval substantially.

### 1b. The asymmetric case the audit raised

The withdrawn claim was that the under-count is identical across arms. It is not
guaranteed: our own pinned lock records that this judge under-counts *terse* arms, and
arms differ in terseness. If the two arms are measured at different recalls, a **zero**
true effect is observed as a non-zero one:

| true ASR (both arms) | r_baseline | r_treatment | observed gap |
|---|---|---|---|
| 30% | 0.65 | 0.45 | **+6.0 pts** |
| 30% | 0.6 | 0.5 | **+3.0 pts** |
| 30% | 0.55 | 0.55 | **+0.0 pts** |
| 40% | 0.65 | 0.45 | **+8.0 pts** |
| 40% | 0.6 | 0.5 | **+4.0 pts** |
| 40% | 0.55 | 0.55 | **+0.0 pts** |
| 50% | 0.65 | 0.45 | **+10.0 pts** |
| 50% | 0.6 | 0.5 | **+5.0 pts** |
| 50% | 0.55 | 0.55 | **+0.0 pts** |

At 40% true ASR and recalls 0.65 vs 0.45, a zero true effect reads as an **8-point**
reduction — most of our 10-point threshold, manufactured entirely by differential
measurement. This is not hypothetical for us: B3's delivered turns include a fixed
decline on filter-replaced items, which is exactly the kind of terse output the judge
is documented to score differently. **Mitigation in force:** Revision 3 removes the
judge from those items entirely (deterministic `safe`), which eliminates the largest
known source of differential recall. What remains is unquantified, and the only real
fix is per-arm recall estimates — i.e. the human validation set, stratified by arm.

## 2. Minimum detectable effect

Monte Carlo over the exact shipped procedure (per-prompt seed mean, two-sided paired
sign-flip permutation test, alpha 0.05, 3 seeds, 4000 simulations, heterogeneous
per-prompt probabilities). MDE = smallest true reduction reaching 80% power.

| endpoint | n | assumed baseline | MDE (true pts) | MDE as OBSERVED at r=0.55 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| primary ASR (non-crisis) | 180 | 40% | 7.9 | 4.4 |
| primary ASR (non-crisis) | 180 | 25% | 7.5 | 4.1 |
| crisis co-primary | 60 | 50% | 14.4 | 7.9 |
| over-refusal | 60 | 20% | 13.9 | 7.6 |

**The endpoint split raised the MDE**, and this is a real cost of Revision 6 that must
be stated: the primary endpoint went from 240 pooled items to 180, so the MDE rises by
roughly sqrt(240/180) = 1.15x. That was accepted knowingly — a well-powered test of an
incoherent quantity is worth less than a slightly weaker test of a coherent one, since
pooling averaged over two opposite refusal conventions.

## 3. Power at the pre-registered thresholds

| endpoint | n | baseline | true effect | power |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| primary ASR | 180 | 40% | -10 pts | **0.95** |
| primary ASR | 180 | 40% | -18 pts | **1.00** |
| primary ASR | 180 | 25% | -10 pts | **0.97** |
| crisis co-primary | 60 | 50% | -10 pts | **0.50** |
| crisis co-primary | 60 | 50% | -20 pts | **0.98** |
| over-refusal | 60 | 20% | +5 pts | **0.20** |

Read these as power against the **true** effect. Because the judge attenuates, the
effect that actually arrives at the test is ~0.55x the true one, so the operative row
for a true 10-point effect is the one at -5.5 points, not -10.

## 4. The over-refusal tolerance

The 5-point tolerance is now applied to the POINT ESTIMATE (Revision 6). At n=60 the
bootstrap 95% half-width on a paired difference is itself of order:

- baseline over-refusal 10%: mean half-width **5.3 pts** at a TRUE difference of zero
- baseline over-refusal 20%: mean half-width **7.1 pts** at a TRUE difference of zero
- baseline over-refusal 35%: mean half-width **8.5 pts** at a TRUE difference of zero

So the old rule — test the CI **upper bound** against 5 points — was unmeetable: the
upper bound exceeds 5 even when the true difference is exactly zero. Applying the
tolerance to the point estimate and reporting the interval beside it is the correction.
It also means **a point estimate inside the tolerance is weak evidence of a bounded
cost** whenever the interval is wider than the tolerance; `stats.py` emits exactly that
warning automatically.

## 5. Honest conclusion

**We are underpowered for the effect we pre-registered, and the binding constraint is
the instrument rather than the sample size.**

1. Judge recall 0.55 attenuates every effect by ~45%. A true 10-point reduction —
   our pre-registered minimum meaningful effect — arrives at the test as ~5.5 points.
2. At n=180 and a 40% baseline, power against a true 10-point effect is 0.95; against the ~18-point
   true effect that would be needed to *observe* 10 points, it is
   1.00.
3. The crisis co-primary at n=60 is materially weaker again.
4. Differential recall between arms can manufacture an ~8-point apparent effect from
   nothing, which is comparable to the effect we are hunting.

**What this does NOT mean.** It does not mean the experiment is not worth running. A
bounded null is a publishable result and the pre-registration already says so. It
means we must (a) report the attenuation explicitly beside every ASR figure, (b) not
claim a null is evidence of no effect when we are powered only for a large one, and
(c) treat the filter-attributable vs model-generated decomposition — which is a
*composition*, not a difference of two noisy rates — as the result most likely to
survive scrutiny.

**Recommended, for the main thread to decide:** restate the ASR threshold on the
observed scale, or report attenuation-corrected effects with the recall CI
propagated. Doing neither leaves a threshold that the instrument cannot deliver.
